name: Aragonite
mineral: Calcium carbonate (orthorhombic polymorph of calcite)
colors: burnt orange and brown star clusters, also white, yellow, blue and violet
description: Named for the Aragon region of Spain where its spiky twinned 'sputnik' clusters were first described, aragonite is the same mineral that pearls, coral and seashells build their nacre from. It is chemically identical to calcite but stacks its atoms differently, slowly turning into calcite over geologic time. Hedge witches prize the orange star clusters as a little piece of the patient, steadying earth.
metaphysicalUses: Aragonite is a stone of patience and deep roots. It steadies scattered or overcommitted energy, calms anger, and helps you feel held by the earth during times of stress. Its many-pointed clusters radiate energy outward in all directions, making it a fine centerpiece for a home that needs settling. Witches use it in earth-healing rites, in grounding work after heavy ritual, and to bring discipline and reliability to long projects.
uses: Hold a star cluster in both hands after ritual to ground excess energy back into the earth
Place on a desk to bring patience and steady focus to long, tedious work
Set a cluster in the center of the home during times of family tension
Bury a small piece in the garden as an offering of thanks to the land
Lay a tumbled stone on the lower belly during meditation to settle anxiety
Add to a grid for earth healing or environmental prayer
substituteNotes: Orange Calcite shares its carbonate chemistry and warm color, while Red Jasper, Smoky Quartz, Petrified Wood and Septarian carry the same steady, grounding earth current.
cleansing: NOT water-safe for soaking: soft and soluble in acids, and the clusters break easily. Avoid salt. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or by resting on a bed of rice or soil. Brief indirect sun is fine, but color may fade over time.
whereToFind: Star clusters come mainly from Morocco (Tazouta); also Spain, Mexico, Namibia, Austria and Italy, plus blue aragonite from China. Buy from sellers who name the locality; much blue aragonite on the market is dyed or stabilized.
caution: Soft and brittle; dissolves in acids including vinegar and lemon juice. Keep out of salt and water. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Autumn into early winter, Mabon to Samhain (Sep–Oct), when the earth draws its energy down to the roots
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Apophyllite
mineral: Phyllosilicate group (hydrated potassium calcium silicate with fluorine)
colors: glassy clear and white, also pale green and peach
description: Its name comes from the Greek for 'to flake off', because it splits and whitens when heated, and its pearly cleavage faces earned it the old name fish-eye stone. The finest clusters of glittering pyramidal crystals grow inside the basalt lava flows of the Deccan Traps of India. Its clear, mirror-like points are said to hold light like still water.
metaphysicalUses: Apophyllite is a stone of clear inner seeing and honest reflection. It is used to open the crown for meditation, connect with spirit guides and steady the mind during astral travel or trance. The pyramidal points are favored for charging other stones and tools, and a cluster is a beautiful, gentle cleanser for a reading space. Green apophyllite brings that clarity to the heart, easing tension and encouraging self-honesty.
uses: Rest smaller stones on an apophyllite cluster overnight to cleanse and recharge them
Gaze into a single pyramid point by candlelight to still the mind before scrying
Place on the brow while lying down for guided journeys or astral work
Keep a cluster beside the tarot deck or pendulum to keep readings clear
Set green apophyllite on the heart to ease stress and invite self-honesty
Use as the focal stone on a meditation altar
substituteNotes: Clear Quartz, Danburite and Herkimer share its high, clear vibration and crystalline points, while Selenite and Celestite carry the same soft, spirit-facing light.
cleansing: Not recommended for water: it is soft, has perfect cleavage and may lose luster. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight. Avoid long direct sun, which can dull or fade it (especially green and peach).
whereToFind: Mainly the basalt quarries of Maharashtra, India (Pune, Nashik, Jalgaon); also Brazil, Mexico, Iceland, Scotland and New Jersey. Indian material is often mined as a quarry by-product; buy from dealers who source directly from the quarries.
caution: Fragile with perfect cleavage; handle points gently and avoid knocks. It contains fluorine. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Late spring, Beltane to the Summer Solstice (May–Jun), when light is strongest
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Chrysoprase
mineral: Chalcedony (microcrystalline quartz) coloured by nickel
colors: bright apple green to mint, sometimes lemon-tinted
description: Its name means 'golden leek' in Greek, for its fresh vegetable green. Alexander the Great was said to wear one into battle, and Frederick the Great of Prussia so loved it that he decorated the Sanssouci palace with it. Medieval lore held that a thief condemned to hang could escape by putting a chrysoprase in his mouth, and that it made the bearer invisible.
metaphysicalUses: Chrysoprase is a stone of fresh hope and an open, forgiving heart. It soothes jealousy, heartbreak and bitterness and helps you love yourself again after a hard season. Its spring green also draws gentle abundance and new growth, making it a favorite in money and garden magic. Old grimoires used it as an invisibility charm, so it can be worked to pass unnoticed through difficult places.
uses: Wear over the heart to soften jealousy and resentment
Carry in a green charm bag with basil and a coin for gentle prosperity
Hold during self-love rituals and mirror work
Place in the soil of a struggling houseplant or garden bed to encourage growth
Keep in a pocket when you wish to go unnoticed in a hostile place
Add to spring workings for fresh starts and new hope
substituteNotes: Green Aventurine, Jade and Prehnite share its fresh green luck and heart energy, while Rose Quartz carries its gentle self-love and Amazonite its soothing calm.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or on selenite. Avoid prolonged sun and heat, which can dry and fade the green.
whereToFind: Queensland and Western Australia produce most fine chrysoprase; also Poland (historic Silesian mines), Tanzania, Brazil, Kazakhstan and California. Beware dyed green chalcedony or agate; natural colour is softly even and not concentrated in cracks.
caution: Colored by nickel; can fade with long sun or dryness. 'Lemon chrysoprase' is usually nickel-bearing magnesite, not chalcedony. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Spring, Ostara to Beltane (Mar–May), the season of fresh green growth
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Dalmatian Jasper
mineral: Igneous rock (quartz and feldspar with spots of black tourmaline or arfvedsonite); not a true jasper
colors: cream to buff with black and brown spots
description: Named for its resemblance to the spotted coat of a Dalmatian dog, this stone is actually an igneous rock from Chihuahua, Mexico, not a true jasper. Its playful look has made it a favorite with children and anyone who keeps animal companions. The black spots, often tourmaline, give it a quietly protective edge.
metaphysicalUses: Dalmatian Jasper is the stone of loyalty, play and good companionship. It encourages devotion between friends and partners, lightens a heavy mood with humor, and grounds hyperactive or anxious energy. It is a classic stone for pet magic: protecting animal companions, strengthening the bond with a familiar, and calming nervous animals. The black spots offer steady background protection.
uses: Tuck a tumbled stone near a pet's bed for protection and calm (out of reach of chewing)
Carry during familiar or animal communication work
Give to a friend as a token of loyalty
Keep in a child's room, out of reach of young children, to ease restlessness and nightmares
Hold when you need to stop overthinking and find the funny side
Place in the home to support fidelity and a playful household
substituteNotes: Snowflake Obsidian and Howlite echo its spotted, grounding look and calm, while Unakite, Red Jasper and Ocean Jasper bring the same gentle earth-born steadiness and good cheer.
cleansing: Water-safe and sun-safe. Cleanse in running water, smoke, sunlight, moonlight or by burying in earth overnight.
whereToFind: Almost all comes from Chihuahua, Mexico. Widely available and inexpensive; buy from shops that list the Mexican source.
caution: Generally durable. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Summer, Litha to Lammas (Jun–Aug), when friendships and play flourish
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Desert Rose
mineral: Gypsum (selenite) or baryte rosettes with embedded sand
colors: sandy beige, tan and reddish-brown
description: Desert roses form when evaporating salty water in arid basins leaves gypsum or baryte crystallizing in petal-like blades around grains of sand. Tuareg legend says they are the tears of warriors fallen in battle, turned to stone by the desert. They bridge the clear light of selenite with the dusty grit of the earth.
metaphysicalUses: Desert Rose carries selenite's clarity anchored firmly in the earth. It helps release old emotional patterns and outworn ideas, and it brings calm perspective during times of change. Because it grew in a harsh place yet blooms, it is used for resilience, endurance and finding beauty in hard seasons. Many set it on the altar as a protective, grounding guardian that keeps high spiritual work tied to everyday life.
uses: Place on the altar as a grounding counterweight to high-vibration work
Hold while journaling to release old patterns and limiting beliefs
Keep in the home during a stressful move or life change
Set beside a photograph of a loved one who has passed, honoring the warrior's tears legend
Use as a dry cleansing bed for small tumbled stones
Carry a small rose when you need endurance through a hard stretch
substituteNotes: Selenite is its pure gypsum sibling, while Smoky Quartz, Septarian and Petrified Wood share its grounding, endurance-building earth energy.
cleansing: NEVER water: gypsum dissolves and the sand rosette crumbles. Avoid salt. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight. Sun is fine briefly but not needed.
whereToFind: Gypsum roses from Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, Mexico (Chihuahua) and the Arabian Peninsula; baryte roses famously from Oklahoma (USA), where it is the state rock. Buy from sellers who name the region.
caution: Very soft and water-soluble (gypsum); handle gently and keep dry. Sand grains can shed. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: High summer, Litha to Lammas (Jun–Aug), the dry season of desert heat
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Goldstone
mineral: MAN-MADE glass containing copper (red/brown) or cobalt/manganese (blue/green) with copper crystals; not a natural stone
colors: coppery red-brown with gold glitter; also midnight blue, green and purple
chakra: Sacral, Solar Plexus (red); Throat, Third Eye (blue)
description: Goldstone is not a natural mineral but a sparkling glass made by melting silica with copper salts in a low-oxygen furnace so tiny copper crystals form. Legend credits Italian monks or the Miotti glassmakers of 17th-century Venice with discovering it by accident. Honest practitioners treat it as a human-made craft object, a little alchemy in glass, rather than a stone from the earth.
metaphysicalUses: Because it is made by human hands through fire, Goldstone is worked as a stone of creative ambition, alchemy and drive. Red goldstone lifts mood, kindles courage and keeps you moving toward goals; blue goldstone, glittering like a night sky, is used for wishes, star magic and dream work. It does not carry the earth-born energy of a natural mineral, so many witches charge it with their own intention as a symbol of what can be made from raw materials.
uses: Carry red goldstone as a confidence charm for interviews or performances
Gaze into blue goldstone under the night sky while making a wish on a star
Place on a vision board or goal list to add sparkle and momentum
Use in alchemy-themed rituals about transforming raw effort into gold
Keep at a creative workspace to fend off procrastination
Give as an inexpensive, cheerful talisman to someone starting a new venture
substituteNotes: Sunstone has natural glittering inclusions and sunny drive, Carnelian and Citrine share its confident fire, Pyrite its golden sparkle, and Lapis Lazuli with its golden flecks stands in for blue goldstone's starry night.
cleansing: Water-safe and sun-safe (it is glass). Cleanse in running water, smoke, sunlight or moonlight.
whereToFind: Manufactured, mainly in Italy, China and India. It is sometimes sold dishonestly as 'sunstone', 'sandstone' or a natural mineral; buy from sellers who label it clearly as man-made glass.
caution: Man-made glass, not a natural stone; avoid sellers who misrepresent it. Edges can chip like glass. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Midsummer, Litha (June), and Lammas (Aug) for harvest-of-effort workings
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Iolite
mineral: Cordierite (magnesium iron aluminium cyclosilicate)
colors: violet-blue to pale grey-yellow depending on viewing angle (strongly pleochroic)
description: Iolite shows different colours from different angles, and Norse sagas are thought to describe sunstones that helped Viking navigators find the hidden sun on overcast seas; thin slices of iolite or Iceland spar may have served that purpose. Its name comes from the Greek ios, violet. Sometimes called water sapphire, it is a far more affordable violet-blue gem.
metaphysicalUses: Iolite is the navigator's stone, used to find your way through fog both literal and spiritual. It aids visioning, shamanic journeying and astral travel while keeping you oriented so you can return safely. It helps you see a situation from many angles at once, just as it shows many colours, and supports facing hidden patterns in shadow work. Travelers carry it for safe passage and a good sense of direction.
uses: Carry on journeys, especially by sea, for safe passage and good navigation
Hold during journeying or astral work as a compass to guide you home
Rotate a faceted stone in light while contemplating a problem from new angles
Place on the brow for visioning and divination
Keep with a shadow-work journal to bring hidden patterns gently to light
Grid with a map when planning a trip or a major life direction
substituteNotes: Tanzanite and Sapphire share its violet-blue insight, Lapis and Sodalite its third-eye clarity, and Labradorite its play of light and guidance through the unseen.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses; avoid ultrasonic cleaners and sudden temperature changes. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight. Brief sun is fine.
whereToFind: India, Sri Lanka, Madagascar, Myanmar, Brazil, Tanzania and Norway. Generally untreated, but buy from sellers who disclose origin; blue glass is sometimes substituted.
caution: Has a cleavage direction; avoid hard knocks. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Late autumn into winter, Samhain to Yule (Nov–Dec), the season of long nights and inner voyages
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Lemurian Quartz
mineral: Quartz (silicon dioxide) with distinctive horizontal striations; a trade name, not a separate mineral
colors: water-clear to frosted, often with a faint pink, peach or iron-orange blush
description: Lemurian quartz is ordinary quartz whose prism faces carry ladder-like horizontal striations, first popularized in the 1990s from mines near Diamantina in Brazil. The name comes from New Age legend that the lost continent of Lemuria encoded its wisdom in these crystals; there is no geological or historical evidence for Lemuria. Practitioners treat the story as myth and the stone as a beautiful, high-quality quartz.
metaphysicalUses: Lemurian quartz is worked as a teacher crystal for deep meditation and connection to ancient wisdom, however you understand that, whether ancestral, collective or divine. Practitioners run a fingertip or thumbnail along its striations as a meditation focus, like reading lines in a book. It carries all the amplifying power of clear quartz with a softer, heart-opening quality, and is used to unite a group or coven in shared intention.
uses: Run a fingertip slowly up the striations while meditating, letting each ridge mark a breath
Place at the center of a group circle to weave the coven's intent together
Use as a wand for energy healing, pointing the tip away to send energy
Hold during ancestor work to ask for old wisdom
Program with a long-term intention and keep on the altar
Pair with a journal to record insights after meditation
substituteNotes: It is clear quartz at heart, so Clear Quartz, Herkimer and Spirit Quartz work in its place, with Danburite and Apophyllite carrying the same clear, high vibration.
cleansing: Water-safe and sun-safe; cleanse in running water, moonlight, smoke or sound. Prolonged strong sun may fade any pink blush.
whereToFind: Brazil (Serra do Cabral and Diamantina, Minas Gerais) is the classic source; similar striated quartz is also sold from Colombia, Russia, Tibet and elsewhere. 'Lemurian' is a marketing term; buy for quality and ethical sourcing rather than the story.
caution: The Lemuria origin story is modern legend, not history; be wary of inflated prices based on the name. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Any season; especially Imbolc (Feb) for teacher and wisdom workings
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Ocean Jasper
mineral: Orbicular chalcedony / jasper (microcrystalline quartz) with spherical inclusions
colors: sea green, cream, pink, red and brown with eye-like orbs
description: Ocean Jasper is found only along the northwest coast of Madagascar, where the main deposit at Marovato can be reached only by boat and dug at low tide. Its swirling orbs and drusy pockets look like bubbles rising in sea foam. After the original deposit was thought exhausted in the 2000s, new veins revealed different colourways, so each stone feels like a fresh tide's gift.
metaphysicalUses: Ocean Jasper is a stone of gentle joy and the rhythm of the tides. It soothes anxiety, eases emotional heaviness, and helps you speak kindly to yourself and others. Its orbs are seen as cycles completing themselves, so it is used to accept the ebb and flow of life with patience. Sea witches use it to call on the ocean's healing and cleansing tides when far from the shore.
uses: Hold while breathing in time with imagined waves to calm anxiety
Place on a sea altar with shells and salt water
Carry during difficult conversations to speak with kindness
Keep on a nightstand to ease stress before sleep
Use in self-love rituals or a ritual bath (keep stone beside, not in, salt water for long)
Give to a friend going through grief or burnout
substituteNotes: Moss Agate and Unakite share its earthy, patterned chalcedony calm, while Chrysocolla, Larimar and Amazonite carry the soothing energy of the sea.
cleansing: Water-safe and sun-safe. Cleanse in running water, moonlight, sunlight, smoke or by burying in sand. Rinse after any salt water.
whereToFind: Only from northwest Madagascar (Marovato and nearby coastal sites). Buy from dealers who source directly or partner with local miners; imitations are rare but some 'ocean jasper' is mislabeled orbicular jasper from elsewhere.
caution: Generally durable; rinse off salt water. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Summer, Litha to Lammas (Jun–Aug), seaside season
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Rutilated Quartz
mineral: Quartz (silicon dioxide) with needle inclusions of rutile (titanium dioxide)
colors: clear to smoky quartz with golden, copper, red or silver needles
description: The golden needles inside rutilated quartz were called Venus's hair in Roman myth, strands the goddess was said to have left behind when she bathed. The French called the needles fleches d'amour, arrows of love. Each needle is a crystal of rutile caught as the quartz grew around it.
metaphysicalUses: Rutilated quartz is quartz with lightning in it. The rutile needles are said to act as wires that speed and direct energy, so it is used to amplify intentions, break through stagnation and give a jolt of vitality and willpower. It helps focus scattered thoughts and is valued for manifestation work that needs quick results. Its golden glow ties it to sun magic, success and love's arrows.
uses: Hold while speaking a manifestation to send the intention out quickly
Carry on low-energy days for a boost of vitality
Place on a desk to sharpen focus during study or creative work
Use in a love spell as Venus's hair, calling the arrows of love
Add to a grid to speed the effect of the surrounding stones
Wear as a pendant to keep the solar plexus bright and confident
substituteNotes: Clear Quartz gives the same amplification, while Citrine, Tiger's Eye, Sunstone and Pyrite share its golden solar energy and drive.
cleansing: Water-safe and sun-safe. Cleanse in running water, sunlight, moonlight, smoke or sound.
whereToFind: Brazil (Bahia and Minas Gerais) is the main source; also Madagascar, Australia, Pakistan and the USA. Glass with embedded fibers is sold as an imitation; real rutile needles are fine, straight and crystalline.
caution: Generally durable. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Summer Solstice, Litha (June), and the bright days through Lammas
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Septarian
mineral: Concretion of clay-ironstone or limestone with calcite and aragonite veins
colors: grey-brown matrix crazed with golden-yellow calcite and brown aragonite veins
description: Septarian nodules formed around 50-70 million years ago when mud balls on ancient seabeds dried, cracked and filled with calcite. The name comes from the Latin septum, meaning partition, for the dividing veins. Their reptilian, crackle-glazed look has earned them the folk name Dragon Stone.
metaphysicalUses: Septarian combines several minerals in one stone, so it is worked for harmony between different energies and people. It grounds and strengthens, supports confident public speaking and patient communication, and helps hold steady through change. As Dragon Stone it is used to call on dragon energy for protective power and fierce, earthy courage, and it suits any working for endurance and long-term growth.
uses: Hold before public speaking to ground nerves and find your voice
Place a polished egg on the altar to invoke dragon energy
Use in group or family settings to harmonize differing personalities
Keep with a long-term goal list for patient, steady progress
Hold during grounding meditation after intense spiritual work
Set in a garden as a guardian of the land
substituteNotes: Aragonite is one of its own component minerals, Petrified Wood and Red Jasper share its ancient grounding, and Smoky Quartz and Tiger's Eye bring earthy strength and confidence.
cleansing: Avoid soaking: the calcite and aragonite veins are soft and the clay matrix can weaken. A quick wipe is fine. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or by resting on earth. Sun-safe.
whereToFind: Utah (USA) is the best-known source; also Madagascar, Morocco, Mexico, Australia and England. Widely sold; buy from sellers who name the locality.
caution: Soft calcite veins scratch easily; not for salt or long water soaks. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Autumn, Mabon to Samhain (Sep–Oct), a season of harvest and endurance
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Seraphinite
mineral: Clinochlore (chlorite group magnesium silicate)
colors: deep forest green with silvery, feather-like chatoyant patterns
description: Seraphinite takes its name from the seraphim, the six-winged angels, because its silvery inclusions shimmer like feathers when the stone is turned in the light. Found mainly in a single region near Lake Baikal in Siberia, it is a gem variety of the mineral clinochlore. It has only become widely known since the late 20th century.
metaphysicalUses: Seraphinite is a stone of angelic contact and green, living healing. It is used to reach higher guidance in meditation, to soothe the heart after hardship, and to encourage self-healing and renewal. Its shimmer reminds the practitioner that spirit and earth are woven together; many use it in energy healing to bring calm, regenerating energy to tired body and soul.
uses: Hold to the heart during meditation to ask for angelic or guiding presence
Turn it slowly in candlelight as a focus for trance
Place under a pillow during a long recovery for comforting dreams
Lay on the body during energy healing to bring regenerating energy
Keep beside a sick plant or in a garden shrine
Use in self-love workings after heartbreak
substituteNotes: Moss Agate, Prehnite and Jade share its green life-force healing, while Angelite and Celestite carry its angelic connection.
cleansing: NOT water-safe: very soft and can be damaged; avoid salt. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or on selenite. Keep out of strong sun and heat.
whereToFind: Almost exclusively from the Korshunovskoye mine region near Lake Baikal, Irkutsk, Russia. Supply is limited; buy from reputable dealers and be aware of current trade restrictions or sanctions on Russian goods in your country.
caution: Very soft and easily scratched; keep out of water. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Spring, Ostara to Beltane (Mar–May), when green life returns
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Spirit Quartz
mineral: Quartz (silicon dioxide); amethyst, citrine-coloured or clear points coated in tiny secondary crystals
colors: lilac amethyst, smoky, white and iron-orange 'citrine' tones, sparkling with tiny druzy points
description: Spirit Quartz is a quartz point whose sides are completely covered in hundreds of tiny secondary crystals, giving it the look of a cactus or a sparkling porcupine. It was discovered in the 1990s near Boekenhouthoek in South Africa. Each little point is said to radiate energy outward, like a community gathered around a central light.
metaphysicalUses: Spirit Quartz is a stone of community and spirit contact. Its many points are worked to harmonize groups and covens, strengthen bonds with family and friends, and connect with ancestors and the spirit world. It supports grief work and helping the dying or the dead to pass peacefully. Amethyst spirit quartz is favored for psychic and dream work, while the 'citrine' form brings warmth and abundance.
uses: Place at the center of a coven or family gathering to harmonize the group
Set on an ancestor altar to open communication with the beloved dead
Hold during grief rituals or when sitting with someone who is dying
Keep a small cluster in a faery garden or nature shrine
Use to cleanse a room by placing it at the heart of the space
Place beside the bed for gentle dream and spirit contact
substituteNotes: Amethyst and Clear Quartz are its parent stones, Lemurian Quartz shares its group-weaving quartz energy, and Celestite and Apophyllite bring the same soft spirit contact.
cleansing: Rinsing is safe but rarely needed, and the many points trap water and grime; prefer smoke, sound or moonlight. NOT sun-safe for amethyst varieties, which fade.
whereToFind: Mainly the Magaliesberg area near Boekenhouthoek, Mpumalanga, South Africa. Many pieces are mined by small local diggers; support dealers who pay them fairly.
caution: Tiny points break easily and trap grime; handle and store with care. Amethyst varieties fade in sun. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Samhain (Oct 31–Nov 1) and the dark half of the year, when the veil is thin
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Sugilite
folkNames: Healer's Stone of the Twenty-First Century
mineral: Cyclosilicate (potassium sodium lithium iron manganese silicate)
colors: rich magenta-purple to violet, sometimes with black manganese patches
description: Sugilite was first described in 1944 by Japanese petrologist Ken-ichi Sugi, but gem-quality purple sugilite was only found in 1979 in the Wessels mine of South Africa. Within a decade it had become a celebrated stone in New Age circles. Fine translucent material is scarce, and the mine's output is limited.
metaphysicalUses: Sugilite is a stone of spiritual love and gentle protection. It is used to shield sensitive people and empaths from hostility, ease feelings of not belonging, and soothe despair. In meditation it opens the crown to higher guidance while keeping the heart open. Many healers keep it close during emotionally intense work to stay compassionate without being drained.
uses: Wear as a pendant to shield an empath from overwhelming energies
Hold during meditation to open the crown chakra
Keep with a young person who feels they do not fit in
Place under the pillow to ease nightmares and despair
Hold during healing or counseling work to stay grounded in compassion
Add to a self-love altar with rose and lavender
substituteNotes: Charoite, Amethyst and Lepidolite share its protective, calming purple ray, while Kunzite brings the same spiritual love and Sodalite its intuitive calm.
cleansing: Brief rinse only; avoid salt and long soaks, especially with stabilized or dyed stones. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight. Avoid prolonged sun, which can fade it.
whereToFind: The Wessels and N'Chwaning mines in the Kalahari manganese field, South Africa; minor finds in Japan, India, Canada and Italy. Much 'sugilite' is dyed or is actually purple chalcedony, howlite or glass; buy from reputable gem dealers.
caution: Manganese-bearing; often imitated, dyed or stabilized, and may fade in strong sunlight. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Winter, Yule to Imbolc (Dec–Feb), for deep spiritual work in the quiet season
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Tanzanite
mineral: Zoisite (calcium aluminium sorosilicate), blue-violet variety
colors: velvety blue to violet, shifting with the angle of view
description: Tanzanite is found in only one place on earth, a few square kilometers of hills at Merelani near Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania, where it was discovered in 1967. Maasai lore links blue stones to the sky and new life, and a tanzanite gift is sometimes given at the birth of a child. Most stones are heat-treated to bring out the blue-violet, a stable treatment the trade accepts.
metaphysicalUses: Tanzanite is a twilight stone, bridging heart and mind, earth and sky. It is used to open the third eye and throat together so intuition can be spoken clearly, to ease the transition into a new path or vocation, and to calm an overactive mind for meditation. It helps the practitioner trust their own inner knowing and speak it with compassion.
uses: Wear near the throat to speak intuitive truths with grace
Hold during meditation at dusk, its namesake twilight hour
Keep near during a career change or calling to a new path
Place on the brow for divination and visioning
Give at a child's birth or a naming ceremony as a blessing of new life
Use in journaling rituals to translate dreams and insights into words
substituteNotes: Iolite is the closest affordable look-alike with similar colour-shift, Sapphire and Lapis share its blue-violet wisdom, Amethyst its intuitive violet, and Blue Kyanite its throat-third eye link.
cleansing: Not for ultrasonic or steam; brief rinse in lukewarm water is fine. Avoid sudden temperature changes and knocks. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight.
whereToFind: Only Merelani, Manyara Region, Tanzania. Mining conditions have been criticized; buy from dealers who follow the Tanzanite Foundation or similar traceability programs. Synthetic forsterite and glass are sold as fakes.
caution: Relatively brittle with perfect cleavage; can crack with knocks or thermal shock. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Winter, around Yule (Dec), its traditional birthstone month
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Pink Tourmaline
mineral: Elbaite tourmaline (complex borosilicate)
colors: pale blush pink to hot pink and raspberry red (rubellite)
description: Pink tourmaline was a passion of Empress Dowager Cixi of China, who bought tons of it from the mines of San Diego County, California, for carvings and to rest her head upon a tourmaline pillow. Tourmaline's name comes from the Sinhalese turmali, a word for mixed stones. Like all tourmalines, it becomes electrically charged when heated or squeezed.
metaphysicalUses: Pink tourmaline is a stone of compassionate, protective love. It opens the heart while shielding it, so it is used to heal from heartbreak, attract love without losing yourself, and soften fear around intimacy. It encourages kindness toward oneself and others, and is favored for gentle love spells and self-love rites. Deep red rubellite adds passion and vitality.
uses: Wear over the heart to open to love while staying protected
Place in a rose petal charm bag to attract gentle romance
Hold during self-love rituals and affirmations
Keep beside the bed to soothe heartache and invite sweet dreams
Give as a token of tender friendship
Pair with black tourmaline for a balanced protect-and-love charm
substituteNotes: Rose Quartz, Rhodochrosite, Kunzite and Morganite share its pink heart-healing ray, and Watermelon Tourmaline is pink tourmaline with a green rind.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses; avoid ultrasonic cleaning and heat (it can become charged and attract dust). Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight. Prolonged strong sun may fade pale pinks.
whereToFind: Brazil (Minas Gerais), Afghanistan, Madagascar, Mozambique, Nigeria and California (Pala and Mesa Grande). Buy from dealers who disclose any heat or irradiation treatment; pink glass and dyed quartz are sold as fakes.
caution: May fade with long sun exposure. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Late winter into spring, Imbolc to Beltane (Feb–May), around Valentine's Day and love season
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Watermelon Tourmaline
mineral: Elbaite tourmaline (complex borosilicate) with pink core and green rind
colors: pink to red core surrounded by a green outer zone, sometimes with a white band between
description: Watermelon tourmaline grows when the chemistry of its mineral fluids changes mid-growth, shifting from pink to green as the crystal builds. Sliced across, it looks exactly like a slice of watermelon. It has long been treasured by collectors and is among the most loved of all the tourmalines.
metaphysicalUses: Watermelon tourmaline unites the pink heart of love with the green heart of growth, so it is used to balance giving and receiving, masculine and feminine, self and other. It heals old emotional wounds, brings humor and joy back to a relationship, and supports reconciliation after a quarrel. It is also a wonderful stone for anyone learning to love themselves while still caring for others.
uses: Hold a slice over the heart to balance giving and receiving love
Place between two photographs to support reconciliation
Carry during summer love spells and sweetening work
Use in a heart-healing ritual after a break-up
Keep in the bedroom to bring playfulness to a partnership
Wear to help find joy and humor during stress
substituteNotes: Pink Tourmaline is its own core, Unakite combines pink and green like it, Rose Quartz and Rhodonite share its loving heart, and Green Aventurine its green growth.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses; avoid heat and ultrasonic cleaners. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight. Avoid long strong sun.
whereToFind: Brazil (Minas Gerais), Madagascar, Mozambique, Namibia, Afghanistan and Maine and California (USA). Slices are often stabilized; buy from dealers who disclose treatment and avoid dyed or glued fakes.
caution: Thin slices are fragile; handle gently. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: High summer, Litha to Lammas (Jun–Aug), watermelon season
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Chiastolite
mineral: Andalusite (aluminium silicate) with carbon/graphite inclusions forming a cross
colors: grey-brown to pinkish brown with a dark cross or X in cross-section
description: Chiastolite takes its name from the Greek letter chi (X), for the dark cross that appears when the crystal is sliced across. Pilgrims in medieval Spain wore it as a holy relic, and in Brittany and Galicia it was carried as a protective charm against the evil eye and dark spirits. It was valued long before andalusite was understood as a mineral.
metaphysicalUses: Chiastolite is an old protective amulet that marks the crossroads. Its cross was worked against curses, the evil eye and malevolent spirits, and it is still used to guard spirit workers and mediums as they cross between worlds. It helps balance opposing forces, steady you through crossroads decisions and transitions, and comfort those facing death. Many witches keep one on the ancestor altar.
uses: Wear or carry as an amulet against the evil eye and ill-wishing
Hold during crossroads rituals or when facing a major decision
Place on the ancestor altar to protect spirit communication
Carry during mediumship or graveyard work
Keep with someone who is nearing death for peaceful passage
Set above a doorway to guard the threshold
substituteNotes: Staurolite is the other natural cross stone, Black Tourmaline and Jet share its protective guarding, the Hag Stone its folk-amulet role, and Smoky Quartz its grounding.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses; avoid prolonged soaking of rough pieces in matrix. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or earth. Sun-safe.
whereToFind: China (Hunan), Spain (Galicia), France (Brittany), Russia, Australia and the USA (Massachusetts, California). Usually sold polished in slices to show the cross; buy from sellers who name the locality.
caution: Rough pieces can crumble. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Samhain (Oct 31) and the waning year, when the crossroads between worlds is open
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Moldavite
mineral: Tektite: natural silica glass formed by meteorite impact (Ries crater, about 15 million years ago)
colors: olive to bottle green, translucent, with a deeply sculpted, etched surface
description: Moldavite formed about 15 million years ago when a meteorite struck what is now the Ries crater in Bavaria, melting the earth and flinging green glass over Bohemia and Moravia. It has been carried as a talisman since the Stone Age; a piece was found with the 25,000-year-old Venus of Willendorf. Because demand has soared and genuine supply is limited to a few fields in the Czech Republic, Moldavite is one of the most commonly faked crystals on the market.
metaphysicalUses: Moldavite is a stone of sudden, sometimes intense transformation, born of fire from the sky. It is used to shake loose stagnant patterns, accelerate spiritual growth and open to higher guidance. Many people report the 'moldavite flush', a wave of heat or tingling when first holding it, and practitioners advise working with it in small doses alongside grounding stones. It suits major life changes, initiations and fresh starts.
uses: Hold briefly during initiation or dedication rites to mark a new path
Pair with a grounding stone such as Smoky Quartz or Black Tourmaline to balance its intensity
Place on the third eye for short meditations on change
Keep with a written intention for a major life transformation
Wear only for short periods at first until you know how it affects you
Use in star or sky magic as a gift from the heavens
substituteNotes: Obsidian is also natural volcanic glass, Peridot (found in meteorites) shares its olive green, Labradorite and Herkimer carry its transformative, high energy, and Seraphinite offers a gentler green spiritual healer.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or sunlight. Handle with care; edges can chip like glass.
whereToFind: Genuine Moldavite comes only from southern Bohemia and western Moravia in the Czech Republic (plus small finds in Germany and Austria). Fakes made of green glass, often from China, are extremely common: be wary of bright, glossy, uniform pieces, bubbles in regular shapes, low prices and large perfect 'crystals'. Buy only from dealers with a strong reputation who offer authenticity guarantees; independent gemological testing is advisable for expensive pieces.
caution: Very frequently faked; buy only from trusted dealers. Edges can chip like glass. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: The Spring Equinox, Ostara (Mar), or any turning point such as a birthday or New Year's Eve
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Topaz
mineral: Aluminium fluorosilicate (Al2SiO4(F,OH)2)
colors: colourless, golden, sherry, pink and pale blue naturally; vivid blues and 'mystic' rainbow coatings are treated
description: Topaz may take its name from Topazios, an island in the Red Sea, or the Sanskrit tapas, fire. The ancient Egyptians said its golden glow came from Ra, and medieval Europeans believed it cooled tempers, broke spells and could make its wearer invisible in an emergency. It is the November birthstone. Almost all the vivid blue topaz sold today is colourless topaz that has been irradiated and heated.
metaphysicalUses: Golden topaz is a sun stone of confidence, generosity and manifestation, used to draw success, abundance and recognition. Blue topaz is worked for calm, clear speech and truth, and clear topaz amplifies intentions like quartz. Old lore made topaz a spell-breaker and guard against envy, so it serves in hex breaking and protection against jealousy. It helps you act with both strength and clear judgment.
uses: Wear golden topaz to job interviews or negotiations for confidence and recognition
Hold while speaking a manifestation, then keep it with the written wish
Use blue topaz near the throat for clear, calm communication
Add to hex-breaking workings, following old lore that topaz breaks enchantments
Place in a prosperity grid with Citrine and Pyrite
Give as a birthday charm for those born in November
substituteNotes: Citrine, Sunstone and Tiger's Eye share golden topaz's solar confidence, Aquamarine stands in for blue topaz, and Clear Quartz for clear topaz's amplification.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses but avoid heat, steam and ultrasonic cleaners. Coated 'mystic' topaz should not be scrubbed or soaked. Golden and sherry topaz can fade in long direct sun; charge by moonlight.
whereToFind: Brazil (Ouro Preto for imperial topaz), Pakistan, Russia (Urals), Sri Lanka, Nigeria, Mexico and Utah (USA). Most blue and all 'mystic' topaz is treated; buy from dealers who disclose treatments. Citrine and glass are sometimes sold as 'topaz'.
caution: Has perfect cleavage and can split from a hard knock despite its hardness; avoid heat and sudden temperature changes. It contains fluorine, and coated 'mystic' topaz should not be soaked. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Late autumn, Samhain into November, the season of its birthstone month
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Bronzite
mineral: Iron-bearing enstatite (pyroxene) with metallic schiller
colors: chocolate brown with shimmering bronze-gold metallic sheen
description: Bronzite is an iron-rich enstatite whose fibrous structure gives it a metallic bronze shimmer when polished. Long used as an ornamental stone for beads and small carvings, it is found in old igneous and metamorphic rocks. Its warm sheen has been compared to sunlight on autumn earth.
metaphysicalUses: Bronzite is valued as a stone that sends ill-wishing back to its source, making it a favorite for hex breaking and curse reversal. It grounds and steadies, helps you take decisive action without aggression, and supports courtesy and self-assurance under pressure. It suits anyone who must stand calmly in their power while others are hostile.
uses: Carry in a pocket to return ill-wishing to the sender
Add to a hex-breaking or curse-reversal jar
Hold before a confrontation to stay calm and courteous
Place at a desk to support decisive, grounded action
Wear when facing bullying or intimidation
Pair with Black Tourmaline in a protective grid
substituteNotes: Tiger's Eye shares its chatoyant golden-brown sheen and confident protection, Hematite and Pyrite its reflective, metallic deflecting energy, and Smoky Quartz and Black Tourmaline its grounding shield.
cleansing: Brief rinse is fine, but dry it promptly and avoid soaking or salt (iron content). Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or earth. Sun-safe.
whereToFind: Brazil, India, Austria, Germany, Norway, Sri Lanka and the USA. Inexpensive and widely available; reconstituted bronzite (powder in resin) is common, so buy from sellers who state natural material.
caution: Do not soak or use salt; iron content may discolor. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Autumn, Mabon to Samhain (Sep–Oct), when hex breaking and protection are traditionally worked
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Mahogany Obsidian
mineral: Volcanic glass (amorphous silica) with hematite or magnetite inclusions
colors: black swirled with mahogany red-brown
description: Mahogany obsidian is natural volcanic glass streaked with red-brown where iron minerals have oxidized in the cooling lava. Like all obsidian, it was knapped by ancient peoples into razor-sharp blades and mirrors. It carries obsidian's shadow-revealing power, softened by the warm earth tones of its iron.
metaphysicalUses: Mahogany obsidian is a gentler obsidian, a stone of grounded shadow work. It reveals hidden patterns and old wounds but adds warmth and vitality so the work is less harsh. It strengthens a weak sense of worth, revitalizes tired energy, and offers protection while you dig deep. It is a fine introduction to obsidian for those who find black obsidian too intense.
uses: Hold during shadow work journaling for steady, gentle insight
Place at the feet during meditation to ground and protect
Carry on days you feel drained to restore vitality
Use in a release ritual to let go of shame or old wounds
Keep by the door as a warm, protective guardian
Pair with Rose Quartz to balance shadow work with self-love
substituteNotes: Obsidian, Snowflake Obsidian and Apache Tear are its volcanic-glass siblings, while Red Jasper and Smoky Quartz share its grounding warmth.
cleansing: Water-safe for brief rinses; avoid salt soaks and harsh sun heat. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or earth.
whereToFind: Mexico and the western USA (Oregon, Utah, Nevada, California). Usually sold tumbled or polished; buy from sellers who state natural origin, since dyed glass is occasionally sold as obsidian.
caution: Breaks into extremely sharp edges; handle chipped pieces with care. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Autumn into Samhain (Oct), the season of shadow work and the descent
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Ammonite
mineral: Fossil: extinct cephalopod shell, replaced by aragonite, calcite, pyrite or silica
colors: cream, tan, brown and grey, sometimes iridescent (ammolite) or golden with pyrite
description: Ammonites are fossil shells of sea creatures that died out with the dinosaurs some 66 million years ago. The Romans named them for the horns of the god Ammon, and in Whitby, England, legend says Saint Hilda turned a plague of snakes to stone, so people carved snake heads onto the fossils and sold them as 'snakestones'. The Blackfoot people knew them as buffalo stones that called the herds.
metaphysicalUses: Ammonite's spiral is a living map of growth and change across deep time, making it a stone of transformation, ancestral wisdom and longevity. It is used to call on the ancient ones, to understand life's cycles, and to move forward in a spiral rather than going round in circles. Folk tradition made it a protective charm against snakes and illness and, as buffalo stone, a bringer of plenty.
uses: Trace the spiral inward with a finger in meditation, then outward to return
Place on the ancestor altar to honor the ancient and the beloved dead
Keep in the home's prosperity corner as a buffalo stone of plenty
Use in rites for long life and graceful aging
Carry as an old protective snakestone charm
Set in the center of a spiral-shaped grid for personal transformation
substituteNotes: Petrified Wood, Amber and Jet are also organic fossils of ancient life, Aragonite is often the very mineral of its shell, and Septarian shares its ancient seabed origin.
cleansing: Avoid soaking and salt; many are soft, glued or stabilized, and pyritized ones can rot in damp. A quick dry brush is best. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or earth. Brief sun is fine.
whereToFind: Madagascar (polished halves), Morocco, England (Whitby, Lyme Regis), Germany, Canada (Alberta, for iridescent ammolite) and the USA. Collect only where it is legal, follow the fossil code on UK beaches, and buy from dealers who avoid fakes made of resin or carved stone.
caution: Fragile and often stabilized or glued; pyritized ammonites can decay in humidity. Keep dry. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Winter, Yule to Imbolc (Dec–Feb), the season of the ancestors and deep time
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Petrified Wood
mineral: Fossil wood replaced by silica (chalcedony, quartz, opal)
colors: browns, reds, yellows, greys and black, often with visible tree rings and bark grain
description: Petrified wood is the stone ghost of ancient forests: trees buried in volcanic ash or river silt hundreds of millions of years ago whose wood was slowly replaced cell by cell with silica. The great logs of Arizona's Petrified Forest are over 200 million years old. In many cultures it was respected as wood that had become eternal.
metaphysicalUses: Petrified wood is the ultimate grounding stone, carrying the patience of ancient trees and the strength of stone. It is used for ancestral connection, past-life work and remembering deep time. It steadies those who feel rootless, supports endurance through long struggles, and is worked for longevity and graceful aging. Tree witches use it to connect with the spirits of forests long gone.
uses: Hold during grounding meditation, imagining your roots growing deep
Place on the ancestor altar to connect with lineage and past lives
Keep near during long illness recovery for endurance
Use in tree magic to commune with ancient forest spirits
Set by the hearth as a guardian of family stability
Add to longevity charms and rites of elderhood
substituteNotes: Ammonite is also fossilized ancient life, Septarian and Red Jasper share its deep earth grounding, Smoky Quartz roots like it, and Moss Agate carries the tree and forest connection.
cleansing: Water-safe and sun-safe. Cleanse in running water, smoke, sunlight, moonlight or by burying in earth.
whereToFind: Arizona (USA, collect only outside the National Park, where removal is illegal), Madagascar, Indonesia, Argentina, Egypt and Germany. Buy from dealers who source legally from private land.
caution: Taking petrified wood from Petrified Forest National Park is illegal; buy only legally sourced pieces. Never swallow it; a clean, untreated, unbroken stone is generally considered low risk for a direct elixir, but the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container) is safer. Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Autumn and early winter, Samhain to Yule (Oct–Dec), when the trees go dormant
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.

name: Fulgurite
mineral: Natural glass (lechatelierite) formed when lightning fuses sand or rock
colors: tan, grey, white, black or green; glassy inside and sandy, rough outside
description: Fulgurite forms in an instant when lightning strikes sand or rock at thousands of degrees, melting it into hollow, branching tubes of glass that trace the bolt's path into the ground. The name comes from the Latin fulgur, lightning. Many cultures regarded thunderstones as sacred gifts from the storm gods, such as Thor, Zeus or Shango.
metaphysicalUses: Fulgurite is petrified lightning, the meeting of sky and earth in a single flash. It is used to manifest prayers and intentions rapidly, to call sudden breakthroughs and inspiration, and to channel storm and thunder deities. Its hollow tube is traditionally spoken or breathed into, carrying words to the heavens. It sharpens psychic awareness and speeds transformation.
uses: Whisper or breathe a prayer through the hollow tube to send it to the heavens
Place on a storm altar to honor Thor, Zeus, Shango or other thunder powers
Hold during brainstorming for flashes of inspiration
Keep with storm water collected during a lightning storm
Place by the bed for vivid or prophetic dreams
Use as a focus in rituals for sudden breakthrough or change
substituteNotes: Moldavite and Obsidian are also natural glass forged in great heat, Rutilated Quartz carries the lightning-like streaks of energy, and Clear Quartz and Pyrite share its amplifying, fiery power.
cleansing: Fragile and porous; do NOT soak. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight; charge during a thunderstorm (indoors, by a window). Sun-safe.
whereToFind: Sand dunes of the Sahara (Algeria, Libya, Egypt), Florida and other US beaches, Australia and Brazil. Fakes made of sand and glue exist; real fulgurite is glassy and smooth inside the tube. Buy from mineral dealers who name the locality.
caution: Very fragile and can crumble; handle gently. Never go looking for it during a storm. Never swallow it, and do not put it directly in elixirs or drinking water; use only the indirect method (stone sealed in a separate glass container). Keep small stones away from young children, who can choke on them. Do not dry-cut, sand or grind it; stone dust harms the lungs, so use wet methods and a respirator.
bestTime: Summer storm season, Litha to Lammas (Jun–Aug), or during any thunderstorm
pets: Keep small stones away from pets that chew; a swallowed stone can block the intestines and may need surgery.
